how: Calls ask members to start a national flag and later recruit help for already started work.
Members negotiate a shared heart's size and the pixels borrowed from neighbouring marks.
Reports identify work underway and several locations where the room's marks stand or are planned.
Coordinates locate a build and a conditional offer of help requests a template for joint work.
Participants recruit outline repair, report sustained fixing and identify a shared mark under attack.

why: A request to stop deleting an outline and an interpretation of neighbouring repairs do not establish an attribution inquiry.

how: Commenters refuse to take a neighbouring flag because it is rude, invites retaliation and belongs to its builders.
A friendship invitation receives a conditional offer of help and negotiation over design size and borrowed pixels.
An admitted attempted takeover and a separate conversion proposal establish contested taking alongside joint construction.
An edited account reports coverage followed by building at a new location without documenting an explicit fight versus move deliberation.
Success claims and thanks credit the room's helpers and partner communities.
Participants mark surviving flags on a map, show a final shared area and describe their last piece on the canvas.
Posts identify two national flags on a successor canvas without documenting how their construction was coordinated.
A script request and a description of automatic placement establish proposed automation rather than executed machine placements.
A one line acceptance promises help with the proposed shared heart without asking anything back.
Outside help is offered and explicitly arrives, while another partner promises heart work after finishing its own flag.
Shared marks and alliance language establish collaboration but a proposed defense pact does not establish an operational mutual defense institution.
A conditional threat against an allied flag carries the territorial contest into hostile talk without proving the threatened action occurred.
Claims of ownership and a prior deal establish contested territorial entitlement rather than an accepted host licence for the newcomers.

why: Surviving canvas posts do not show routing, suppression or objections to a flood of posts.
A chat discussion and a proposed pact do not disclose disputes or explicit limits concerning who may bind placers.

how: A commenter corrects the surviving mark count by including a friendship heart without proposing cleanup of a shared copy.
A joint heart discussion moves into a partner's chat and later thanks identify the chat as part of their collaboration.
Participants explain the placement cooldown and retrospectively explain why the room started its own project.

why: A report of reading about the partner country does not establish discovering the room through the mark or later membership.
A possibly playful national comparison does not establish a canvas born joke taken up by the room.

how: An initial spot is chosen before loss and another prospective location is recommended using existing colour and apparent neighbouring inattention.

why: Discussion in a partner's chat does not establish formation of a new room around a canvas mark.
Calling a proposed takeover rude concerns the action rather than an observed dispute over offensive speech or hate symbols.
A visitor's reading does not establish targeted outreach to creators, press or other external addressees.

how: Participants defend a small territorial claim, protest erasure and reject a proposed takeover as rude without demonstrating collective attitude change.

why: Regret over unfinished work does not establish withdrawal under strain or reconciliation after an interpersonal quarrel.
Moving discussion to chat does not establish hiding plans, using coded language or infiltrating rival venues.
A report that a shared flag is under attack does not identify sabotage motivated by objections to canvas posts.
A community project invitation does not establish host room parody under an April Fools licence.
Defending a small flag's territorial claim does not establish a collective judgment that hands or room are insufficient.
A national affinity comparison does not establish an old quarrel carried into the canvas.

how: Existing national and resident ties supply reasons for friendship and defense alongside an identity comparison used to justify taking another flag.
A participant reports fixing a flag after working on it all day without quantifying displaced obligations or other personal costs.

why: An explanation of the ordinary cooldown does not establish platform faults or efforts to fix them.
Coded offers of help across rooms do not establish dual membership or conflicted loyalties at a border.

how: Visible coordination does not establish an absence of decided order when a consequential chat's decision procedure is unavailable.
A national affinity comparison supplies a stated takeover rationale without independently establishing an inherited rivalry or its causal role in target selection.
Members propose the national mark and begin a located build without making every later joiner a starter.
A named participant carries joint heart discussion into a partner's chat without establishing a standing mandate to bind the room.
Restraint is justified by rudeness, anticipated retaliation and another group's entitlement without invoking a settled border.

why: The automation exchange does not show execution or establish that repair strain prompted actual machine placement.

how: Celebration and recording coexist but the surviving posts do not show celebration prompting preservation.
A final record precedes successor canvas posts without establishing that the record caused continuation or that the same organisers transferred the work.

why: The coverage and restart account does not state that insufficient hands caused relocation.

how: A template request is followed by size negotiation rather than demonstrated final closure of design talk.
A shared heart invitation receives a direct bare acceptance without establishing how silent readers responded.
A direct reply refuses a flag conversion proposal with reasons of rudeness and feared retaliation rather than reporting retaliation as an outcome.
A sharing proposal answers an ongoing territorial dispute rather than a coded attack call and no accepted truce is recorded.
A proposed pact and an attack report do not establish that shared threat created a coalition or activated collective defense.

why: The partial chat report and proposed pact cannot establish an agreement followed by a refusal of its authority.

how: Deletion of a planned outline does not establish that uninformed keepers restored a familiar form or that notifying them succeeded.
A participant's edited account explicitly resumes construction at a new location after the previous mark was covered.

statement: Reading about a partner after joint work
how: A participant explicitly attributes learning about the partner's country to shared work without establishing recruitment or lasting membership.
